implementerProof.how: I re-ran the implementer's command, `cd packages/pi-legion && LEGION_TEST_OMP=$TMPDIR/omp-pin/omp-v18.12.2-sami.20261026-135627-linux-x64/bin/omp LEGION_TEST_NATS_URL=nats://127.0.0.1:15337 bun test ./extensions/controller-start-omp.test.ts`: 12 pass, 0 fail. In pi-envoy, `bun run test` gave 1468 pass, then 9 pass. I re-ran its control: with markStartupTurnPending removed from handleSessionStart, the case 'before /legion-controller-start runs' fails, because the first request's last message is the card and not the start message. I restored the file and checked it with cmp. Its proof holds for the cases it covers. The failures below are cases it does not cover.

failures.criterion: A5 ('a card read mid-run gets no extra turn') and architect round-5 item 1 ('one turn for it'): a startup card that a turn after the start turn reads gets no further wake.
failures.evidence: Red test 'a startup card that a turn after the start turn reads gets no second wake' in packages/pi-legion/extensions/controller-start-omp.test.ts (commit 1c8a078a) fails at f0fb9ec9. To see it: `cd packages/pi-legion && LEGION_TEST_OMP=<pinned omp> LEGION_TEST_NATS_URL=<nats> bun test ./extensions/controller-start-omp.test.ts -t "no second wake"`. It expects no model request after the 2nd and receives one, whose last message is the wake. Cause: card-wake.ts adds a startup card seen while the mark held to #owed, and #check counts owed cards as unread whatever the branch shows. So a turn after the start turn that read the card (here the turn a card published during the start turn gets; in scratch case C1, a controller notice's turn) is followed by '2 Envoy messages above arrived with no turn to read them' and a 3rd request. Evidence: https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/2278#issuecomment-6477452232

failures.criterion: Architect round-5 item 4 and the spec's 'a card that reaches an idle session still starts a turn': the pending start mark cannot hold cards forever.
failures.evidence: Red tests 'a startup card held by an unsent start mark gets its turn when the start claim never answers' and '... when the start command never runs' (commit 1c8a078a) both fail at f0fb9ec9 with 'no model request within 90 s' (the bound is 3 x STARTUP_TURN_CAP_MS). To see them: `bun test ./extensions/controller-start-omp.test.ts -t "unsent start mark"` in packages/pi-legion. Cause: #startTurnHold returns STARTUP_TURN_CAP_MS for every check while sentAt is undefined, so the check re-arms with no end. The mark is cleared only by the session's first agent_start, its shutdown, or a claim that fails or hands over. A register request that never settles (the daemon client sets no timeout) and a launch without /legion-controller-start do none of these. In scratch runs, no request came within 95 s; the card was read only after the operator typed a prompt. A refused claim (403) does release the card, but its wake came 29967 ms after the refusal, at the next poll.
